question: Which uterotonic agent is recommended as the drug of choice for active management of the third stage of labour (AMTSL) to prevent postpartum haemorrhage?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ergometrine causes sustained, tetanic uterine contraction and also constricts blood vessels (risk of hypertension). It is not the first choice in AMTSL, especially in women with hypertension.
Correct! Oxytocin (10 IU IM or slow IV infusion) is the WHO-recommended first-line uterotonic for AMTSL. It produces rhythmic contractions, has rapid onset, and is well tolerated.
Misoprostol is an alternative in settings where oxytocin is unavailable (no refrigeration needed), but it has more side effects (fever, shivering). Oxytocin remains first choice where available.
Salbutamol is a uterine RELAXANT (tocolytic), not a stimulant. It would worsen, not prevent, postpartum haemorrhage.

overallFeedback.feedback: Oxytocin (10 IU IM) is the WHO-endorsed first-line agent for AMTSL. Ergometrine and misoprostol are alternatives or adjuncts when oxytocin is unavailable or insufficient.
Correct! Oxytocin is the cornerstone of active management of the third stage and the primary prevention of PPH.
